title: The Coming Wave
subtitle: Technology, Power, and the Twenty-first Century's Greatest Dilemma
pitch: A DeepMind co-founder, now running Microsoft AI, argues that AI and synthetic biology will spread like every technology before them, and that we must find a way to contain them anyway.

chapters.g: A short opening that sets the stakes of the coming wave.
Suleyman admits the uncomfortable starting point: history says powerful technologies always spread.
From fire to the printing press to cars, technologies get cheaper and spread everywhere.
What it would mean to keep a technology under control, and why it has almost never worked.
The rise of modern AI, from DeepMind's game playing systems to large language models.
Synthetic biology: gene editing, DNA synthesis and the power to design living things.
Robotics, quantum computing, new energy and other technologies riding the same wave.

chapters.t: Four features of the coming wave
chapters.g: What makes this wave different: asymmetric impact, hyper evolution, omni use and autonomy.
Why no one stops: national pride, profit, curiosity and the fear of falling behind.
The deal between citizens and the nation state, and how the wave threatens it.
How the wave makes attacks, misinformation, accidents and job shocks easier and bigger.
Two bad paths: states that fragment and lose control, or states that turn to surveillance and authoritarian control.
The core dilemma: both openness and lockdown lead to danger. There is a narrow path between them.
Suleyman argues we have no choice but to try, and that partial containment has worked before.
Ten layers, from technical safety and audits to choke points, critics, business incentives, governments, alliances, culture and movements.
A closing look at what a contained, beneficial wave could make possible.

ideas: Technologies tend to proliferate, so containment is the central challenge.
AI and synthetic biology are omni use and can act autonomously.
Incentives make it very hard for anyone to slow down alone.
We need layered containment, from code to culture.

args.a: Containment is hard but must be possible.
args.c: Some say the book's own history argues containment will fail. Others argue it understates existential risk from AI specifically.

args.a: Choke points, like advanced chips, give us leverage.
args.c: Choke points can erode as technology spreads and as other countries build their own supply chains.

questions: Suleyman builds AI while warning about it. Does that make his warning more or less credible to you?
Which of the ten steps is most realistic in your country?
What does 'pessimism aversion' mean, and do you see it in yourself?

quiz.q: What does Suleyman call the central challenge?
quiz.w: Containment means keeping powerful technology under meaningful control.

quiz.q: Which two technologies lead the coming wave?
quiz.w: He calls them the technology of intelligence and the technology of life.

quiz.q: What is the dilemma in Part III?
o: Too many rules or too few
Openness risks catastrophe, lockdown risks dystopia
